To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ER status did not predict superior survival in women with breast cancer who carried a germline mutation in BRCA2; 2) oophorectomies were associated with reduced risk of death in these women; and 3) chemotherapy did not predict superior breast cancer survival in these women.

For women with breast cancers and a germlines BRCA2 mutation positive ER status does no predict superior survival, Oophorectony is associated with a reduction in the risk of death from Breast cancer and should be consider in the treatment plan.

for women with a BRAC2 mutation, positive estrogen receptor (ER) status is not associated with a reduced breast cancer mortality risk, and bilateral oophoreectomy is associated with a 55% reduced breast cancer mortality rate.

the development of novel and more effective therapies for the treatment of breast cancer, particularly for the subgroups of breast cancer patients who are at the highest risk of recurrence and death.
the identification of the most important prognostic factors and treatment strategies for breast cancer.

bilateral oophoreectomy is associated with reduced risk of death due to breast cancer, but not due to other causes, and that the effect is independent of the effect of chemotherapy.
the risk of death from BC for BRCA2 mutation carriers is significantly decreased with bilateral oophoreectomy and the use of adjuvant chemotherapy.
the presence of a BRCA2 germline mutation is not associated with a poor prognosis in breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women with breast cancer with a BRCA mutation should have bilateral salpingo oophorectomies.
oophorectomecy is the most important treatment in BRCA2 mutation carriers with breast cancer and that the effect of chemotherapy is less important.
women with a BRCAA2 mutation who are treated with a bilateral oophrectomy have superior breast cancer survival compared to women who do not have an ophorectomy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oophorectomies should be offered to women who are BRCA2 positive and have breast cancer.
women with a BRAC2 mutation who have breast cancer should consider having bilateral oophoreectomy, which is a relatively simple and low cost procedure.
oophorectomies should be considered as part of the treatment for women with breast cancer who have a germline mutation of BRCA2.
